**RE: Appeal of denial dated August 15, 2026 — Reference number POC-6A6D9C61F2-98168**
**Member:** Jordan Grant | **Member ID:** W874343567
**Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
**Governing policy:** *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* — https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's denial of the lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 15, 2026 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision. I believe the records already submitted address the plan's own criteria in *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)*, and I have set out below how each point matches what is in my chart.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Spondylolisthesis with segmental instability.** The policy states:

> "Spondylolisthesis with segmental instability confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI), with associated symptomatic unremitting low back pain, radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication, when either of the following criteria are met"

My imaging of July 18, 2026 — MRI of the lumbar spine together with flexion-extension radiographs — shows grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. I have had nine months of progressive pain in my lower back and legs that is not relieved by rest. My examination documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. I cannot stand or walk more than ten minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, and sitting relieves it.

**2. The dynamic-instability threshold the plan itself sets.** The policy states:

> "Radiographic documentation dynamic instability of at least 4 mm of translation or 10 degrees of angular motion on dynamic imaging that has failed 6 weeks of conservative management"

My flexion-extension radiographs of July 18, 2026 document 5 mm of translation. My conservative care ran from April 24, 2026 through July 3, 2026 — supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 20 visits over 10 weeks, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is longer than the six weeks the policy names, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**3. Spinal stenosis with anterolisthesis.** The policy also states:

> "Spinal stenosis, where criteria for lumbar decompression in Section I.C. above are met, and any of the following is met: Decompression is performed in an area of segmental instability as manifested by gross movement on flexion-extension radiographs; or Decompression coincides with any degree of anterolisthesis (grades I, II, III, IV or V))"

My records document severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina, movement on flexion-extension radiographs, and grade I anterolisthesis at L4-L5. I was not given the text of Section I.C., so I cannot map my records to it line by line. If Aetna's decision turned on Section I.C., I ask that the reviewer identify that criterion specifically so it can be addressed with the exact records it calls for.

**4. Conservative measures.** The policy states:

> "Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression."

All of my conservative care is recent and falls within the past year:

- **Active physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy, core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, April 24, 2026 to July 3, 2026, 20 visits completed, documented in the discharge note.
- **Medications:** NSAIDs for six months, with inadequate relief.
- **Additional treatment:** corticosteroid injection on May 9, 2026, which gave about four weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned.

If Aetna needs a separate record of any other item listed in that paragraph, I ask that it be named, and I will ask Dr. Duval's office to send it.

**5. Surgeon's examination.** The policy states:

> "Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon."

The prior authorization packet includes examination findings: neurogenic claudication, diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, and no bowel or bladder dysfunction. Dr. Duval is my operating surgeon and has documented that this procedure is needed. If confirmation of the examining or reviewing clinician is what was missing, that is a single document, and I ask that it be identified so my surgeon can provide it rather than the request being denied outright.

## A note on the other criteria in the policy

*CPB 0743* also lists indications for adult scoliosis, lumbar pseudarthrosis, flatback syndrome, spinal fracture, pars defects in members under 18, spinal infection, and spinal tumor, and a hemoglobin A1C provision for members who are diabetic. Those describe different clinical situations from mine, and I am not relying on them. My request rests on the spondylolisthesis-with-instability and spinal-stenosis criteria quoted above. For general surgical readiness, my records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

The policy excerpts available to me also refer to further conditions and lists that were not reproduced in what I have. I am not able to respond to criteria I have not been shown.

## What I am asking for

The denial says the documentation was incomplete, but it does not say which document or which criterion was missing. I am asking Aetna to:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize CPT 22612 based on the records already submitted; or
2. If the file is still considered incomplete, identify in writing the specific criterion from *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* that was applied and the specific document needed, so my surgeon's office can send it promptly.

I would also like a copy of the clinical criteria used in this review and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination.

Per the notice, this appeal must be received by February 11, 2027. I am submitting it with Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, by fax to 859-425-3379 and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed before sending. Aetna's member line is 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am in pain, my walking is limited, and my surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed. I would appreciate a written decision as soon as the plan is able to provide one.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Grant**
